source_quality.notes: text layer covers all 29 pages; the deficit definitions and the logistic were checked on the raster

task_reconstruction: Define water deficit as withdrawal over renewable supply, split it by sector, project Egypt to 2030 with and without climate change, and test five measures.

section_map.summary: summary of the deficit, the forecast and the five measures
the thresholds and the two kinds of scarcity
the split of inflow and outflow
the intervention and its modeled effect
the fitted figures and the yearly tables

contributions.summary: a deficit defined as withdrawal over renewable supply, unsustainable above one
a baseline the detailed forecast is measured against
a climate-adjusted forecast of 161 percent by 2030
five measures that bring the deficit down to 78 percent

dependency_graph.relation: the indicator is what the split rewrites
the deficit is what the renewal terms correct
population drives the agricultural and residential terms
the simple projection is what the detailed one is compared with

assumptions.summary: consumed water leaves the system and nothing is stored
factory efficiency and the mix of goods stay constant
livestock and aquaculture are negligible beside irrigation
renewable inflow stays at 57.3 cubic kilometers
recycling stays constant until the plan changes it

data_and_preprocessing.summary: population from 1962 to 2013 fitted to a logistic
industrial water taken from one 1997 study after estimates disagreed
crop yield set at 0.262 megatonnes per million people
household water fitted on three years

models.summary: deficit as withdrawal over renewable supply
inflow and outflow split into named parts
the deficit after recycling and artificial supply
industrial water as a logarithm of GDP
agricultural water from crop need and irrigation loss
a baseline of falling use per person

verification.summary: the detailed forecast set against the baseline
climate change turned on, moving 2030 by four points
each measure run separately and its saving reported

results_trace.summary: with climate change the deficit reaches 161 percent by 2030
the five measures bring it to 78 percent and save 484 cubic kilometers

writing_logic.summary: the summary concedes the reader's privilege before the crisis
the threshold is derived from the definition
the weaknesses name the inputs that break the model
every recommendation serves the same ratio

language_observations.summary: flags an assumption as counterintuitive before defending it
keeps a contradicted proxy and says so
distrusts the R-squared the thin data produce
sets the unchecked 161 against the treated 78

visualization_observations.summary: a diagram splits inflow and outflow into named branches
the population fit is plotted against the record
the industrial equation and its R-squared are printed on the figure
yearly tables carry the forecast through 2030

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: admitting an assumption feels wrong before defending it reads as careful
showing the input that makes the model negative reads as honest

weaknesses.summary: the deficit is once described as scarce when negative, against its own definition
both fitted curves give negative water outside a narrow range
GDP is kept as the indicator after the data contradict it
the climate adjustment is never written as a formula

independent_extensions.summary: define stress as a ratio of withdrawal to renewable supply and mark the point it passes one
run each proposed measure on its own and report what it saves

unresolved_questions: the prose once says scarcity begins when the deficit is negative
the growth rate and midpoint of the population logistic are not printed
the climate adjustment between model 1 and model 2 is never written out
the ten megatonne import target is chosen rather than derived
the yearly tables in the body and the appendix do not line up
